medicines.name: Paracetamol 650
medicines.title: Paracetamol 650: Uses, Dose, Side Effects
medicines.metaDescription: Paracetamol 650 (Dolo, Crocin, Calpol) for Indian homes — what it treats, safe adult dose, max per day, side effects, brands and indicative prices.
medicines.tagline: The safest default for fever and everyday pain — as long as you respect the daily cap.
benefits: Gentlest common painkiller on the stomach — no food needed first
Safe first choice in dengue-season fevers, unlike NSAIDs
Works for both fever and pain, so one strip covers most households
Decades of safety data at label doses
sideSerious: Overdose is silent and hits the liver — never exceed 4 tablets in 24 hours
Yellowing eyes/skin, dark urine — stop and see a doctor
Rash with swelling of face or throat — emergency
cautions: Cold-and-flu combos (D'Cold, Cheston Cold) already contain paracetamol — count them toward the daily 3 g
Regular alcohol use, liver disease or low body weight shrinks the safe margin — ask a doctor first
Fever beyond 3 days on paracetamol is a doctor visit, not a higher dose

medicines.name: Ibuprofen 400
medicines.title: Ibuprofen 400: Uses, Dose, Side Effects
medicines.metaDescription: Ibuprofen 400 (Brufen) — when it beats paracetamol, safe adult dosing after food, who must avoid it, side effects, Indian brands and indicative prices.
medicines.tagline: The anti-inflammatory workhorse — stronger on swelling than paracetamol, harder on the stomach.
benefits: Reduces inflammation, not just pain — better for sprains and swollen joints
Often stronger than paracetamol for period pain and dental pain
Short-acting, so occasional use clears the body quickly
sideSerious: Black stools or vomiting blood — stop immediately, emergency
Swelling, breathlessness or reduced urination — kidney warning
Wheezing in asthmatics — avoid if aspirin-sensitive
cautions: Never on an empty stomach — always after food or milk
Avoid entirely in suspected dengue or any bleeding disorder
Skip it if you have ulcers, kidney disease, uncontrolled BP or heart failure
Don't combine with other NSAIDs (diclofenac, aspirin) — the risks stack

medicines.name: Diclofenac gel
medicines.title: Diclofenac Gel: Uses & Side Effects
medicines.metaDescription: Diclofenac pain-relief gel (Volini, Voveran Emulgel) — how to apply it for muscle and joint pain, side effects, cautions, brands and indicative prices.
medicines.tagline: An NSAID you rub on instead of swallowing — pain relief where it hurts, with less stomach risk.

quick.Adult dose*: Thin layer on the painful area

benefits: Acts locally — far less of the drug reaches your stomach and kidneys
Good first option for localised pain before reaching for tablets
Easy to combine with rest and ice/heat therapy
sideCommon: Mild itching or redness where applied
sideSerious: Widespread rash or blistering — stop and see a doctor
Wheezing or breathlessness after use — NSAID sensitivity
cautions: Not on broken, infected or eczema-affected skin
Wash hands after applying; keep away from eyes and mouth
Don't stack with full-dose oral NSAIDs without asking a doctor
Cover from direct sun — treated skin burns faster

medicines.name: WHO-ORS
medicines.title: WHO-ORS (Electral): How to Use It Right
medicines.metaDescription: WHO-ORS (Electral) — the most life-saving OTC item in India. How to mix it correctly, when to use it, why ORSL tetra packs don't count, brands and prices.
medicines.tagline: The most life-saving thing in your medicine drawer — if you mix it right and pick the real one.

quick.Mix: 1 large sachet in 1 L clean water

benefits: Replaces water AND salts in the exact ratio the gut absorbs best
Reduces the need for IV drips in most home diarrhoea cases
Safe for all ages when mixed correctly — including children
Costs less than ₹25 per litre of protection
sideCommon: Mild nausea if gulped too fast
sideSerious: Vomiting everything for over 6 hours — needs a doctor
No urine for 8+ hours, sunken eyes, drowsiness — emergency dehydration signs
cautions: ORSL, Rebalanz and similar tetra packs are fruit drinks — NOT WHO-ORS. Look for 'WHO-ORS' on the sachet
Never mix in less water to make it 'stronger' — wrong concentration harms
Kidney or heart patients on fluid restriction should ask a doctor first
Pair with zinc for children's diarrhoea (doctor-guided)

medicines.name: Antacid gel
medicines.title: Antacid Gel (Digene): Uses & Cautions
medicines.metaDescription: Antacid gels and tablets (Digene, Gelusil) — how they neutralise acidity, correct dose, side effects, medicine interactions, brands and indicative prices.
medicines.tagline: Neutralises acid on contact — honest relief for occasional acidity, a mask for chronic reflux.
benefits: Fastest common relief for meal-related acidity — works in minutes
Simethicone in most Indian formulas also breaks up gas
Doesn't need absorption into the blood — acts inside the stomach
sideSerious: Kidney patients can accumulate aluminium/magnesium — ask a doctor
Black or tarry stools are NOT from antacids — see a doctor
cautions: Needing antacids beyond 2 weeks means see a doctor, not buy a bigger bottle
Take other medicines 2 hours apart — antacids block absorption of many drugs
Recurring night-time reflux or difficulty swallowing needs proper evaluation

medicines.name: Fruit salt (ENO)
medicines.salt: Sodium bicarbonate + citric acid + sodium carbonate
medicines.title: ENO Fruit Salt: Uses, Dose & Cautions
medicines.metaDescription: ENO fruit salt — how the fizz neutralises acid in minutes, correct dose, why the sodium matters for BP and heart patients, and indicative prices.
medicines.tagline: Instant fizz for occasional heartburn — with a sodium load your blood pressure notices.
benefits: Among the fastest OTC acidity fixes — relief in minutes
Single-use sachets travel well
No drowsiness, no interactions with most medicines at occasional use
sideSerious: Regular use adds significant sodium — risky with high BP, heart or kidney disease
Swelling of feet or sudden BP spikes with frequent use — stop and see a doctor
cautions: It's a rescue, not a routine — daily acidity needs a doctor, not daily ENO
On a salt-restricted diet (BP, heart, kidney, pregnancy-induced hypertension)? Ask first
Wait for the fizz to settle before drinking to avoid gulping gas

medicines.name: Isabgol
medicines.title: Isabgol: Uses, Dose & Side Effects
medicines.metaDescription: Isabgol (psyllium husk) for constipation — how the fibre bulk-former works, correct dose with water, side effects, cautions, brands and indicative prices.
medicines.tagline: A fibre, not a drug — the gentlest fix for constipation, as long as the water glass is full.

quick.Adult dose*: 1–2 tsp in a full glass of water

benefits: Not habit-forming, unlike stimulant laxatives
Works with your gut's own rhythm — softens and bulks stool naturally
Also steadies mild loose motions by absorbing excess water
Modest LDL-cholesterol benefit with regular use
sideCommon: Bloating or gas in the first days
sideSerious: Taken with too little water it can swell and choke or block — always a FULL glass
Severe abdominal pain, vomiting or no stool + no gas — possible obstruction, emergency
cautions: Never take dry or with a sip — minimum one full glass (250 ml) of water
Skip it during severe abdominal pain or suspected blockage
Take other medicines 1–2 hours apart — fibre can slow their absorption
Diabetics: some flavoured brands carry added sugar — check the label

medicines.name: Loperamide 2 mg
medicines.title: Loperamide 2 mg: Uses & Warnings
medicines.metaDescription: Loperamide (Imodium, Eldoper) for acute watery diarrhoea — when it's appropriate, strict adult dosing, when it's dangerous, brands and indicative prices.
medicines.tagline: Stops the runs when you can't stop — but the wrong situation makes it genuinely dangerous.
uses: Work situations where a toilet isn't reachable
benefits: Slows the gut fast — buys you a safe journey or meeting
Single capsules work; no course needed
Pairs with ORS, which remains the actual treatment
sideSerious: NEVER with fever or blood in stool (dysentery) — it traps the infection inside
Severe bloating or constipation after use — possible ileus, see a doctor
High doses affect heart rhythm — never exceed the label
cautions: Not for children — paediatric diarrhoea is ORS + zinc + doctor
Maximum 2 days of self-use — diarrhoea persisting beyond that needs a doctor
Rehydration with ORS comes first; loperamide only manages the symptom
Skip it if diarrhoea started right after antibiotics — ask a doctor

medicines.name: Cetirizine 10 mg
medicines.title: Cetirizine 10 mg: Uses & Side Effects
medicines.metaDescription: Cetirizine 10 mg (Okacet, Cetzine, Alerid) — allergy, sneezing and hives relief, correct adult dose, drowsiness warning, brands and indicative prices.
medicines.tagline: One tablet, most allergies quieted for a day — just don't plan on driving right after.
benefits: 24-hour cover from a single tablet
Less sedating than older antihistamines like chlorpheniramine — though not zero
Also calms itchy skin reactions, not just the nose
sideSerious: Confusion or urinary retention in the elderly — use with care
A true allergic emergency (throat swelling, breathlessness) needs a hospital, not a tablet
cautions: Skip driving and machinery until you know how sleepy it makes you
Alcohol multiplies the drowsiness — avoid the combination
Allergy 'season' lasting beyond 2–3 weeks of self-dosing deserves a doctor's look
Pregnancy and breastfeeding — ask a doctor first

medicines.name: Cold combo tablets
medicines.title: Cold Combo Tablets: What's Inside
medicines.metaDescription: Cold combination tablets (D'Cold Total, Cheston Cold) — what's actually inside, the paracetamol-stacking trap, who should avoid them, brands and prices.
medicines.tagline: Three drugs in one tablet — convenient, effective, and the easiest way to accidentally double-dose paracetamol.
benefits: One tablet covers fever, congestion and runny nose together
Cheaper than buying three separate medicines for a short cold
Night doses help you actually sleep through a cold
sideSerious: Stacking with Dolo/Crocin overdoses paracetamol — count every source toward 3 g/day
Palpitations or severe restlessness — stop and see a doctor
cautions: Check the composition on the strip — most already contain 325–650 mg paracetamol
High BP, heart disease, thyroid, glaucoma or prostate trouble? Ask a doctor before decongestants
A cold is viral — antibiotics don't help; 5–7 days of rest and fluids do
Avoid alcohol; drowsiness stacks

medicines.name: Menthol-camphor balm
medicines.title: Vicks & Menthol Balms: Safe Use
medicines.metaDescription: Menthol-camphor balms (Vicks VapoRub, Amrutanjan) — blocked-nose and headache relief done safely, child-safety warnings, brands and indicative prices.
medicines.tagline: The smell of every Indian winter — safe comfort for adults, with real rules around small children.
benefits: Instant sensory relief that helps sleep through a cold
No tablets, no interactions with other medicines
One tin serves the whole family's adults for months
sideCommon: Skin irritation or burning on sensitive skin
sideSerious: Camphor is poisonous if swallowed — keep away from children
On or under an infant's nostrils it can trigger breathing distress — never do this
cautions: Not for children under 2 at all; for older children, chest and back only
Never inside the nose, on broken skin, or near the eyes
It comforts symptoms — it doesn't shorten the cold; persistent cough needs a doctor

medicines.name: Povidone-iodine
medicines.title: Povidone-Iodine (Betadine): First Aid
medicines.metaDescription: Povidone-iodine (Betadine) antiseptic — cleaning cuts, scrapes and minor burns correctly, when a wound needs a doctor, brands and indicative prices.
medicines.tagline: The brown bottle that guards every Indian first-aid box — for wounds you can see the bottom of.
benefits: Broad germ kill — bacteria, fungi and viruses on the skin surface
Ointment form stays put on a bandaged wound
Decades of first-aid track record; easy to use correctly
sideSerious: Allergy — hives, swelling, worsening redness: stop and see a doctor
Large-area or long-term use can affect thyroid function — ask a doctor
cautions: Clean the wound with running water FIRST — antiseptic isn't a substitute for cleaning
Deep, dirty, gaping or animal-bite wounds need a doctor and possibly a tetanus shot
Thyroid disorders, pregnancy or breastfeeding — check before regular use
A wound getting redder, warmer or oozier after 2 days is infected — doctor

medicines.name: Clotrimazole 1%
medicines.title: Clotrimazole Cream: Uses & Dose
medicines.metaDescription: Clotrimazole 1% cream (Candid, Canesten) for ringworm and fungal itch — correct duration, why steroid-combo creams backfire, brands and indicative prices.
medicines.tagline: The honest answer to ringworm — if you use it long enough and skip the steroid-combo shortcuts.

quick.Use*: Thin layer over + 2 cm beyond the patch

benefits: Treats the infection itself, not just the itch
Well tolerated on most skin, including skin folds
Cheap, widely available, and effective when the full course is completed
sideCommon: Mild burning or redness in the first applications
sideSerious: Rash spreading or blistering despite 2 weeks of correct use — see a doctor (may need oral therapy)
cautions: Avoid steroid-antifungal combo creams (widely misused in India) — they hide the rash while the fungus spreads
Stopping when the itch stops = relapse; continue 1 week beyond visible clearing
Keep the area dry — fungus thrives in Indian humidity; loose cotton helps
Everyone in the house with a patch should treat at the same time; don't share towels

medicines.name: Calamine lotion
medicines.title: Calamine Lotion: Uses & Side Effects
medicines.metaDescription: Calamine lotion for prickly heat, itchy rashes, insect bites and chickenpox itch — how to use it, when a rash needs a doctor, brands and indicative prices.
medicines.tagline: The pink bottle for angry skin — cools, dries and calms most everyday itches.

quick.Use*: Shake well, dab on with cotton

benefits: Cools on contact and takes the edge off scratching
Gentle enough for children's chickenpox itch
No drug interactions — it works on the surface
sideSerious: A rash that spreads, blisters or comes with fever isn't a calamine job — see a doctor
cautions: Skin only — never on eyes, mouth or broken, oozing skin
If itch persists beyond a week of use, get the rash diagnosed
Moisturise between applications if skin over-dries
